Title: MyCC: Cartel whistleblowers to get stronger protection, rewards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) will strengthen protection and provide rewards to whistleblowers who provide information on cartel activities or bid-rigging practices.
This follows amendments to the Competition Act 2010 and the Competition Commission Act 2010.
MyCC chief executive officer Datuk Iskandar Ismail said stronger protection was crucial as cartel activities typically occurred secretly and behind the scenes, requiring the cooperation of whistleblowers connected to companies or consumers.
"Previously, protection did exist, but it was insufficient. Now we are further enhancing the protection in addition to providing rewards.
"There were complainants who came forward to provide information previously, but when no reward was given, they left," he said during the Ruang Bicara programme on Bernama TV today.
He said complainants also faced the risk of losing their jobs if they disclosed confidential company information, which was one of the factors making them reluctant to come forward.
"The complainants said that they were risking themselves to come to MyCC, yet no compensation would be given to them should they lose their job for leaking company secrets," he said.
Iskandar said, once the amendments are gazetted this year, MyCC will be able to provide more comprehensive protection to individuals who come forward with information.
He said the move would also make it easier for the public, particularly consumers, to lodge complaints regarding anti-competitive practices.
"Now that there is protection, when we enforce these (amendments) this year, it will be easy for everyone, especially consumers, to make complaints.
"At the same time, we will continue to conduct advocacy programmes for consumers every month," he said.
In this regard, MyCC is inviting individuals or companies with information on cartels to lodge complaints through various channels, including WhatsApp.
Iskandar said the amendments also expanded MyCC's role in conducting market studies that have a significant impact on the people, including in the digital economy and e-commerce sectors.
He said MyCC will now have the power to conduct market studies on sectors affecting consumers.
He said cooperation with competition agencies in other countries also enabled MyCC to obtain information to ensure the domestic market did not fall victim to anti-competitive practices by international companies.

Title: N. Korea defections sink amid Kim's crackdown
Article:
A BUILDING-SIZED  North Korean flag waves from a tower on the de facto border with South Korea, marking territory that experts say has become nearly impossible to escape.
The combined total of North Koreans to reach South Korea in the past six years is less than the number that typically defected each year for decades — and appears to be declining further this year.
The main cause is leader Kim Jong-un's aim to preserve his family dynasty by sealing the country off from the outside, keeping people in and information out, experts say.
"As I understand it, bringing family members directly from North Korea is currently impossible," said  Chae Yoon-seo, 29, who fled in 2019.
She swam across a river into China at night with a smuggler's help, and travelled through Laos, Vietnam and Thailand before finally flying to South Korea.
Defections to the South hit a peak of more than 2,900 in 2009 and stayed well above 1,000 per year for the next decade.
But there were just 63 in the first half of this year — down by over a third from the same period last year, said Seoul's Unification Ministry.
Arrivals have fluctuated over the decades, but plunged sharply during the Covid-19 pandemic when many nations shut their borders.
A key change in North Korea, however, started years before.
After taking power in 2011, Kim began restricting the informal trade and migration links along the roughly 1,415km northern border with China.
In addition to being an economic lifeline, the Chinese border region has also been the first step in most defectors' escapes.
The long frontier was relatively porous, unlike the heavily mined, fenced and surveilled Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that serves as the Koreas' de facto border.
Along the boundary with China, Kim's government has erected fences and installed cameras as well as strips of sand that preserve the footprints of anyone who crosses.
"North Koreans built a real Soviet-style border security system," said Andrei Lankov, an expert on the North at Kookmin University in Seoul.
Beijing has helped too, said Lankov, noting China's preference to keep the status quo of the Kim dynasty by opposing potential instability from defectors or their supporters.
The roughly 34,500 defectors to reach the South since 1998 are a fraction of North Korea's 26.6 million people, United Nations figures show, but the plunging number of escapes has consequences.
"Defectors are the main source of information about the North," said Fyodor Tertitsky, lecturer at Seoul's Korea University, noting both South Korean intelligence and researchers interrogate them.
Though some people still do get out.
Defector Gyuri Kang's 2023 escape by boat with her mother and aunt — across the maritime border with the South, an extremely rare feat — was a "miracle", she told a UN hearing.
She is also a case in point for why North Korea has made great efforts to seal itself off.
Kang noted the influence of South Korean dramas smuggled in on USB drives, finding them "more credible than North Korea state propaganda".
"North Korean authorities are keenly aware of the impact of outside media," she said.
In 2020, North Korea made possessing foreign media a crime punishable by years-long forced labour terms — and potential death sentences for large-scale distribution, according to Amnesty International.
Lankov, from Kookmin University, said external information is the greatest threat to the long-term survival of North Korea's leadership.
"If they let their people interact with the outside world, they are highly likely to be overthrown, and maybe killed or driven into exile," he added.
Chae, the defector, said she hoped the North's isolated people would  not one day simply be forgotten by the outside world.
"These days, there are a lot of cynical reactions on helping other countries, so I am a bit worried that one day, interest in North Korean human rights might fade away as well," she added.
The writers are from AFP

Title: China-Malaysia ties reach new heights after three major elevations - Outgoing ambassador
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: China-Malaysia relations have undergone three major elevations over the past five years, culminating in a high-level strategic community with a shared future, outgoing China's Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing said.
He said bilateral ties had progressed from a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to a China-Malaysia community with a shared future, before being further elevated to their current status.
"These three monumental strides have brought China-Malaysia relations to a new level and opened up broader prospects for cooperation between our two countries," he said at a reception marking the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China and the conclusion of his five-year tenure in Malaysia.
Ouyang said Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Malaysia in April marked another milestone in bilateral ties, ushering in what he described as a new "Golden 50 Years" for China-Malaysia relations.
"The visit has driven bilateral relations into their best period in history and provided important strategic guidance for the future development of China-Malaysia ties," he said.
He said the momentum had continued through high-level exchanges, including Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's recent visit to China.
"His Excellency's meeting with Premier Li Qiang yielded important new consensus for deepening win-win cooperation between our two countries," Ouyang said.
International Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani was the guest of honour at the event, representing the Malaysian government.
Also present were Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook and Bernama's chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin.
Turning to economic cooperation, Ouyang said growing trade and investment ties remained a source of inspiration to him, with bilateral trade rising from US$131.16 billion in 2020 to nearly US$200 billion in 2025.
China has remained Malaysia's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years and continues to be a major source of foreign investment, he said.
Ouyang also highlighted progress on the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), which is now more than 95 per cent complete and targeted for completion by the end of this year.
He said the "Two Countries, Twin Parks" initiative continued to support businesses in both countries, while Malaysia's second 5G network, supported by Chinese technological expertise, was expanding connectivity nationwide.
Cooperation in emerging technologies, including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), data centres and electric vehicles (EVs), was also contributing to the economic transformation and upgrading of both countries, he said.
"China and Malaysia are far more than traditional trade partners. We are pioneering a vanguard model for regional cooperation in new quality productive forces," Ouyang said.

Title: Married couple killed in Tampin crash
Article:
TAMPIN: A married couple died in an accident involving two vehicles on Jalan Gemencheh today.
District police chief superintendent Amiruddien Sariman said that in the 10.55am incident, the 26-year-old woman, who was the front passenger in a Proton Wira car, died at the scene, while her 27-year-old husband, who was the driver of the car, was pronounced dead at the Gemencheh Klinik Kesihatan.
He said the accident occurred when the car the victims were in was travelling from Gemencheh to Bukit Rokan, while the other vehicle, a Perodua Bezza was coming from Bukit Rokan heading towards Gemencheh.
"Upon arriving at the scene, the car driven by the victim was believed to have lost control before entering the opposite lane and colliding with the Perodua Bezza.
"Due to the incident, the couple was confirmed dead while their four-year-old son was injured and taken to the Tampin Hospital for further treatment," he said in a statement today.
Amiruddien said the bodies of both victims were taken to the Tampin Hospital's forensic unit for an autopsy to determine the cause of death.
Those with information regarding the accident are requested to contact the traffic police at the Tampin district police headquarters at 06-441 2502 or the investigating officer Inspector Imanul Hassan Mohamad Shah.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: US says no China arms sale plans after envoy cites Trump offer
Article:
WASHINGTON: The United States said Monday that it has no plans to sell arms to China, after a US envoy said President Donald Trump asked Xi Jinping if he would like to buy American weapons.
US Ambassador to China David Perdue said Trump made the extraordinary offer to sell arms to the rival superpower in response to Chinese concerns over weapons sales to Taiwan.
Trump's proposal came during Chinese President Xi's pomp-filled state visit to the White House last week, Perdue told Fox News.
"President Trump continues to say, 'Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world.' He actually asked President Xi – would he like to buy some? – at one point," Perdue said in an interview.
"There are continuing conversations about other sales, (Trump) and President Xi talk about that every time they get together," Perdue said, adding that the US position has not changed.
The White House said no such sales to China were in the pipeline.
"The US government has no plans to sell weapons to China," a US official told AFP.
US arms sales to Taiwan, the self-ruled island which China claims is part of its territory and has threatened to seize by force, have long been a thorny issue between Washington and Beijing.
The United States is required by law to supply Taiwan, which has a democratically elected president and legislature, with weapons for its defence.
'Negotiating chip'
The US State Department said in a statement to the New York Times that "US law prohibits arms sales to China and there is no offer or plan to sell arms to China."
The Chinese foreign ministry did not directly answer when asked about the comments on Monday, but said China has "always strengthened its national defence capabilities based on its own needs, and remains committed to maintaining world peace and stability."
Beijing warned Taiwan in June that seeking independence "by relying on the United States or through military means is a dead end."
Trump has maintained a strategically ambiguous stance over Taiwan, refusing to say directly whether the US would come to its aid if China invades, while continuing to approve weapons sales.
Washington approved a US$11.1 billion arms sale to Taiwan in December, which Perdue said was a sale of "more arms to Taiwan than any other president since 1979."
The US paused a US$14 billion weapons purchase by Taiwan in May, with Trump calling it a "very good negotiating chip" in dealings with China, raising fears that Taiwan's security could be traded away.
During his Washington trip, Xi repeated his warning that Trump should show "prudence" over Taiwan, and went further to urge the United States to oppose Taiwan independence explicitly.
Trump has declined to say whether he discussed Taiwan with Xi during the visit, preferring to stress what he says is his good relationship with the Chinese leader as the two countries seek to manage their tensions.
The two leaders have met twice already this year, with Trump having travelled to Beijing in May.
They have confirmed they will meet for a third and fourth time at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, in November and the G20 forum at Trump's Doral resort in Miami in December.

Title: NST Leader: UN veto power under fire as calls for reform intensify
Article:
VETO is the Latin word for "I forbid" or "I prohibit",   derived from the Latin verb
vetare
conceived during the 494BC revolt in ancient Rome against the unjust actions or laws of ruling aristocratic magistrates.
In what is known as the First Secession of the Plebs, plebeians formed the Tribune of the Plebs  to protect or rescue their class from arbitrary and unfair arrest, punishment or judgment, usually with laws equivalent to Roman authority.
Later expanding to 10 members, the tribune became legally and religiously inviolable but its authority was capped within Rome's city limits.
Under the system, antagonists who harmed a tribune were executed on the spot without trial. Sounds familiar? Now, 2,440 years into the future, this system  has evolved into the United Nations and, more crucially, the 15-member Security Council (UNSC).
Unlike in ancient times, the five superpowers of the United States, Russia (then the Soviet Union), China, the United Kingdom and France have commandeered the UNSC.
Before the UN became fully operational, at the 1945 San Francisco Conference a bloc of small and medium-sized nations, led by Australian politician H.V. Evatt,  opposed the veto, warning of institutional paralysis.
At the start of his  premiership in 1981, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad initiated the first Malaysian opposition to the veto, a foreign policy  position maintained by his successors.
Last week at the UN General Assembly, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan reemphasised this policy, imploring that the veto must be questioned and firmly challenged, particularly its support of crimes against humanity.
Urging stronger accountability over its use, Mohamad pointed out that expanding the UNSC's membership was pointless but judged that its paralysis should not dislocate the UN's viability.
The five superpowers' rationale in justifying veto power is not democratic fairness but pragmatism.   Russia, including the now-defunct Soviet Union, has used it the most at 131 times, mostly during the Cold War to block Western-backed resolutions.
The US has invoked the veto 89 times, mostly to block resolutions critical of or restricting Israel, followed by the UK (29), mostly to deal with African colonial issues.   At 21 times, China has jointly invoked the veto together with Russia over resolutions involving Syria and the Middle East.
At 16 times, France has not imposed a veto since 1989, reflecting its advocacy of restraint.   Having been invoked 286 times  since 1945, the veto has been used as a "power tool" on matters of survival, life and death.
Theoretically, the veto can be cancelled but this needs two-thirds of UNGA members to vote on a resolution to amend Article 108 of the UN Charter.
Realistically, the vote serves no purpose  as the five permanent members would stymie it.     Malaysia can only condemn the undemocratic and anachronistic veto but for now, Mohamad's  statement remains a global rallying call.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US, Iran set to hold separate talks with mediators on Monday or Tuesday
Article:
UNITED STATES: Qatari mediators are likely to hold separate talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in New York and with the US side on Monday or Tuesday, an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters, in a fresh push to end the war.
The talks are expected to focus on an amended version of a seven-day proposal that Iran presented last week on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Araqchi remains in New York after attending the General Assembly. It was not immediately clear who would represent the US side in the talks with mediators.
Iran's semi-official ISNA news agency later confirmed that Araqchi would meet the mediators in the US on Monday morning, New York time.
The two sides will "examine the latest proposals and views regarding the current situation", ISNA added.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei told state media later on Monday that Araqchi's stay in New York had not been extended and that the foreign minister would return to Teheran according to his original schedule.
Baghaei made no comment on the talks with mediators.
Trump has flagged further talks this week
Iran's seven-day plan envisages an end to all hostilities in Iran and Lebanon, the unfreezing of billions of dollars' worth of Iranian assets, an end to sanctions on Iranian oil and the lifting of the US blockade on Iranian ports.
Teheran would then allow the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and the two sides would also resume talks on Iran's nuclear programme.
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected Iran's proposal, saying Teheran wanted a swift agreement because of the crippling economic pressure it is under.
However, he also told Axios on Sunday that he expected US negotiators to engage in further talks this week.
Araqchi said on Sunday that mediators had not formally conveyed a US rejection to Teheran and that Iran was awaiting Washington's definitive position before deciding its next steps.
"Our conditions are clear, and any move towards reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met," he said on Sunday, adding that only a negotiated solution could resolve the impasse.

Title: Two men held on NSE with 690kg ketum leaves in car
Article:
IPOH: Two men were arrested after allegedly possessing 690kg of ketum leaves in a car at Km371 of the North-South Expressway (NSE) southbound early yesterday.
Muallim district police chief superintendent Khalid Mohamad said the suspects, aged 21 and 31, were arrested by a team from the Highway Patrol (EMPV) Sectors 7 and 8, Northern Zone 4, Bukit Aman Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (TEID) about 2am.
He said the two suspects were believed to be runners supplying ketum leaves for the local market.
"An inspection of the Toyota Alphard found 69 black plastic packages containing suspected ketum leaves weighing an estimated 690kg, with an estimated market value of RM27,600," he said in a statement today.
Police also seized the vehicle and a remote-control key for investigation purposes.
Khalid said preliminary checks found that the first suspect had a record of one drug-related offence and five criminal offences, while the second had two drug-related offences and one criminal offence.
They are being detained to assist investigations under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM congratulates national contingent on best-ever WSC Shanghai performance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated the Malaysian contingent for winning one bronze medal and 13 Medallions for Excellence at the WorldSkills Competition (WSC) Shanghai 2026.
Anwar said the achievement was the national contingent's best performance in the competition since 1995.
"Congratulations to the 22 youths who demonstrated their prowess and skills in TVET (Technical and Vocational Education and Training), bringing honour to the country.
"Continue to hone your skills and pursue excellence. You are the pride of the nation," he said in a Facebook post today.
In the same post, the prime minister gave special recognition to Sia Xin Wan, who won a bronze medal in the Software Testing category and received the Best of Nation award.
At WSC Shanghai 2026, the Malaysian contingent of 22 participants competed in 21 skill categories across various technical sectors supervised by the Department of Skills Development and the Ministry of Works.
The tournament ran from Sept 22 to 27 and brought together 1,400 skilled young professionals from 65 countries and regions competing in 64 skill areas.

Title: China's ambassador to Malaysia praises warmth, kindness of Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has become his second home after almost six years in the country, said outgoing China's Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing.
Ouyang, who is wrapping up his tenure as China's 16th ambassador to Malaysia, said Malaysia was where he had lived and worked the longest outside China.
"Malaysia is where I have lived and worked the longest outside China. It has truly become my second home," he said at a reception hosted by the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Malaysia to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China and bid farewell to him.
Present at the event were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching and Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong.
Also present were Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul and Senate President Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah.
Ouyang said he had travelled to all states during his nearly six years in Malaysia, allowing him to gain a deeper understanding of the country's history, culture and traditions.
"From the bustling cities to the quiet towns and villages, along the way I have been immersed in the rich tapestry of Malaysia's history, culture, and traditions, gaining a profound understanding of this beautiful country and its tender-hearted people," he said.
He said Malaysian friends often asked him what he thought of the country.
"I always tell them Malaysia is a country of beauty: beautiful landscapes, beautiful people, and most important of all, beautiful hearts.
"This is not diplomatic courtesy; it is my genuine, deep-seated feeling," he said.
Ouyang said he had been deeply moved by the warmth, kindness and affinity towards China shown by Malaysians from various walks of life.
He said these included government, Parliament, military, business and civil society leaders, as well as ordinary Malaysians he met in parks, on the streets and at local eateries.
"All of this fills me with even greater conviction in the bright future of China-Malaysia relations," he said.
Reflecting on his tenure, Ouyang said he felt "deeply honoured and privileged" to have witnessed China-Malaysia relations reach new heights.
He said exchanges between the two governments, parliaments and political parties had become closer, while bilateral ties had progressed from a comprehensive strategic partnership to a China-Malaysia community with a shared future and now towards a high-level strategic community with a shared future.
Ouyang also highlighted the strong economic and people-to-people ties between the two countries, including cooperation in trade, technology, education and tourism.
He said the close ties between the two peoples were particularly evident during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Malaysians extended assistance to China at the beginning of the outbreak, followed by China's support for Malaysia during subsequent waves of the pandemic.
As he prepares to return to China, Ouyang said he would continue to support the development of China-Malaysia relations.
"As the 16th Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia, it is the honour of a lifetime to contribute my part to deepening bilateral cooperation and bringing the hearts of our two peoples closer together.
"No matter where the future takes me, a piece of my heart will always remain in Malaysia, and I will forever champion the enduring growth of China-Malaysia relations."
Ouyang also expressed his gratitude to Malaysian friends from all walks of life, the Chinese-Malaysian community, Chinese nationals, enterprises and institutions in Malaysia for their support during his tenure.
"I look forward to the day our paths cross again," he said.

Title: Seoul says North Korean mines 'highly suspected' as cause of DMZ blast
Article:
SEOUL: A blast that injured three South Korean military officers inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) last week was likely caused by North Korean landmines, Seoul's military said Monday.
The DMZ is a 248km long and roughly 4km-wide buffer zone that has divided the Korean Peninsula since the 1953 armistice.
While the zone itself is officially demilitarised, its northern and southern boundaries are among the world's most heavily fortified frontiers and remain littered with landmines.
With no peace treaty signed, Seoul and Pyongyang technically remain at war.
The preliminary findings of a joint probe with the United Nations Command into the Sept 21 explosion suggested that "recently planted mines" were involved, Kwon Dae-won, vice chairman of South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff, said at a live briefing.
"The mines exploded at a location about 10m south of the Military Demarcation Line, and we have confirmed that the site was about 10m from an area where changes in the terrain were observed and where North Korean forces are believed to have recently planted mines," he said.
"Taking into account the crater and the pattern of the flames from the explosion, the extent of the injuries sustained by the service members... we assess that North Korean landmines are highly suspected to have caused the blast."
Kwon said two landmines exploded and that a third, unexploded mine was found while soldiers were withdrawing after the blast.
The three officers suffered severe injuries in the explosion, including one who lost his foot.
'All options on the table'
The ongoing investigation found that while the exploded landmines used TNT – a substance also used in South Korean mines – they displayed characteristics different from domestic landmines, including the absence of "metal fragments", the Joint Chiefs of Staff said.
And while South Korean landmines have a lethal radius of around 20 metres or more, the blast radius of the mines that exploded last week was relatively small, it added.
Once completed, should the probe conclude that nuclear-armed Pyongyang was responsible, "North Korea would bear full responsibility for the incident, and our military will take appropriate and corresponding measures," Kwon said, without giving further details.
Whether the North Korean mines were deliberately planted or had drifted would be determined by the final investigation, said Joint Chiefs of Staff director of operations Yang Jin-hyeok.
"All necessary options are on the table" in deciding what measures to take once final results are available, he told the briefing.
South Korea and the UN Command have inspected the area inside the DMZ where the incident took place.
Since 2024, after North Korean leader Kim Jong Un designated South Korea as his country's "principal enemy", Pyongyang's military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off.
Landmine incidents have previously heightened tensions between the two Koreas.
In 2015, two South Korean soldiers were seriously wounded when a landmine exploded on the southern side of the DMZ, with one losing both legs.
Seoul concluded that North Korean troops had crossed the Military Demarcation Line to plant the mines, an accusation Pyongyang denied.
The incident prompted South Korea to resume anti-Pyongyang loudspeaker broadcasts along the border.

Title: 5 Malaysians nabbed in Jakarta for smuggling drugs in their shoes
Article:
JAKARTA: Five Malaysians were detained by the Indonesian police (Polri) Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) on Friday for smuggling 5kg of the synthetic drug etomidate concealed in their shoes.
The five were stopped by Indonesia's Customs and Excise authorities at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after arriving from Kuala Lumpur on an AirAsia flight before being handed over to Bareskrim policemen.
Polri Narcotics Eradication Division director General Eko Hadi Santoso said the suspects were searched after Indonesian Customs and Excise officers became suspicious of the movements of the five individuals.
He said a search of the five found that each had hidden two packets of a white powder in the insoles of their shoes, with each packet weighing about 500g.
"In total, there were 10 packets weighing about 5kg," he said in a statement published by CNN Indonesia today.
Investigations revealed that the five were under the "control" of an individual who used the name "Madam" in the Telegram communications application.
Upon arrival in Jakarta, they were to go to a hotel in Harmoni, in central Jakarta, and put their shoes in a red coloured bag.
They were told to hand the bag to a certain 25-year-old Chinese citizen in the lobby of the hotel.
Based on this information, Bareskrim arrested the Chinese citizen and found the keys to an apartment in Mediterania Marina Residence in north Jakarta.
A raid on the apartment revealed that it was being used as a laboratory to produce vape pods containing etomidate, a short-acting intravenous anaesthetic.
Police seized seized various raw materials and equipment for assembling vape pods, including 16 five-litre jerry cans of flavouring liquid, five one-litre bottles of liquid, 21,000 empty vape pods and 15,000 silicone pod caps.
Also seized were 800 plastic pipettes and 4,715 pod containers in various flavours.
Eko said the Chinese citizen was believed to have been in Indonesia since September and had been staying at the apartment.
He said the man admitted to receiving instructions through a communication group on the "Signal" app to record the inventory.
Police estimate the seizures to be worth 127.5 Rupiah (about RM33.8 million).
In July, a
Malaysian pilot
was arrested at the same airport for smuggling a large quantity of drugs, including more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg into Indonesia.
Earlier this month, Malaysian police arrested a
second pilot
in the Klang Valley.
The second pilot was believed to have been involved in the flow of cash between the drug syndicate and the first pilot.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign leaders pay tribute to Siti Hasmah's medical, public health legacy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Condolences from foreign leaders continued to pour in following the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, with tributes highlighting her lifelong contributions to medicine, public health and social welfare.
Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari expressed deep sorrow over her passing and extended his heartfelt condolences to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, his family and the people of Malaysia.
"Dr Siti Hasmah's long and distinguished service in medicine, public health and social welfare would be remembered with respect," Zardari said, according to Pakistan's Press Information Department (PID).
Meanwhile, Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu also expressed deep sadness, paying tribute to Dr Siti Hasmah as one of Malaysia's first women doctors and highlighting her contributions to maternal health and the development of women in rural areas.
He said her leadership in gender equality and family welfare reflected a lifelong commitment to serving the community and empowering future generations.
Muizzu extended his condolences to Dr Mahathir and his family on behalf of the government and people of the Maldives.
Meanwhile, Cambodian Senate President Hun Sen described Dr Siti Hasmah as a respected doctor, public health advocate and a pioneer who devoted her life to serving Malaysians.
"In this time of profound grief, on behalf of the Senate of Cambodia and myself, I would like to extend my deepest sympathy and heartfelt condolences to you, your family, the government and the people of Malaysia," Hun Sen, who is also Cambodia's Acting Head of State, said in a Facebook post.
The former Cambodian prime minister also highlighted Dr Siti Hasmah's advocacy for maternal health, literacy, drug abuse prevention and mental health, as well as her role in the modernisation of Malaysia's healthcare.
"She and her legacy will be remembered for many generations to come," he said.
Dr Siti Hasmah was
laid to rest
at 6.20pm at Pusara Negara in Precinct 20, Putrajaya. Her husband, Dr Mahathir, their children, and other family members were present.
A state-level funeral was held to honour the wife of the former prime minister, who died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) at 9.20am Monday at the age of 100.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore's former leaders remember Siti Hasmah's warmth, grace
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore's former leaders have remembered the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali for her warmth, grace and lifelong contributions to the well-being of Malaysians.
They also extended their condolences to former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family.
Dr Siti Hasmah
died
at the National Heart Institute (IJN) in Kuala Lumpur at the age of 100. She was laid to rest at Pusara Negara, Precinct 20 here at 6.20pm on Monday, with Dr Mahathir Mohamad, their children and family members present.
Singapore Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong remembered Dr Siti Hasmah as a warm and gracious person who was full of life and had a wonderful sense of humour.
Lee, in expressing his condolences to Dr Mahathir and family, said Dr Siti Hasmah, as a doctor, had devoted much of her life to improving the health and well-being of Malaysians, particularly women, children and families.
"Ho Ching and I will remember Tun Siti Hasmah fondly," he said in his Facebook post on Monday.
Lee also fondly recalled his interaction with Dr Siti Hasmah about her love for music and the violin.
"I remember speaking to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah about her violin performance at the Istana Budaya, when she played for a good cause.
"She continued performing well into her 90s, including to raise funds for charity. Her zest for life was remarkable," he said.
Former prime minister Goh Chok Tong, meanwhile, described Dr Siti Hasmah as a remarkable woman with many achievements.
Goh said he came to know her through his official engagements with Dr Mahathir in Malaysia and Singapore, as well as at Asean, APEC, Commonwealth Heads of Government and other international gatherings.
"We will always remember her for her grace, sincerity and warm friendship," he said in a Facebook post.
Former Singapore president Halimah Yacob described Dr Siti Hasmah as warm, friendly and humble, recalling an encounter during her presidency that left a lasting impression on her.
"She held my arm and said that she was so proud to have met the female President of Singapore. Simple kind words of encouragement, solidarity and support seared in my memory," she wrote in a Facebook post.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shuhaily remembers Siti Hasmah as a 'mother' to security personnel
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Former Federal Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain remembers Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali as a "mother" who cared for the security personnel assigned to protect her and Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Shuhaily, who served on the couple's security detail during several assignments, including overseas trips, said Dr Siti Hasmah would make it a point to check on the team's welfare.
"Every now and then, when I was assigned to such duties, at the end of every assignment, every day she would ask us, 'Have you eaten?', 'Do you have enough rest?' or whatsoever.
"To us, who were involved in the detail, she was like a mother to us," he said after Dr Siti Hasmah was laid to rest at the National Cemetery in Presint 20, earlier today.
Shuhaily, who shared the same birthday as Dr Siti Hasmah, highlighted a celebration the two had together in Baltimore, United States, "sometime in 2012 or 2013."
He said Dr Siti Hasmah invited him to join her and Dr Mahathir for a birthday celebration.
"She said, 'Shuhaily, your birthday is the same as mine, right?' I said, 'Yes, Tun.'
"She asked Tun M to sit on my right and she was on my left. The three of us held the knife and cut the cake together. That is a memory I will never forget," he said.
Shuhaily said Dr Siti Hasmah continued to remember him whenever they met, even years after the celebration.
He was also the leading the security detail during Dr Mahathir's return to the international stage after becoming prime minister for the second time, including his first visit to the United Nations.
"To see Tun come back to the international platform was always an honour. The welcome that he received after so long was still there.
"Tun Siti Hasmah was the strong supporter of the man himself. It is a loss to the country," he said.
Dr Siti Hasmah, 100, died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) in Kuala Lumpur this morning.
She was laid to rest beside the late Tun Endon Mahmood, wife of former prime minister Tun Abdullah Ahmad Badawi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar remembers 'Kak Hasmah' as gentle, loving mother figure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim remembers the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali as a gentle and loving maternal figure, as well as a close friend and confidante to him and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
Anwar said the nation would continue to remember Dr Siti Hasmah's services and contributions, describing her as a motherly figure who treated everyone with affection and made them feel close to her and valued.
He said it was difficult for him and Dr Wan Azizah to accept her passing, especially as the fond memories they shared continued to return to their minds.
"Together with Azizah, I came to pay our last respects to Kak Hasmah, a maternal figure whose gentleness and affection we will always remember, as well as a friend and close companion over the years," he said in a Facebook post today.
The post was accompanied by photographs of him and his wife paying their respects and meeting her husband, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Anwar and Dr Wan Azizah also prayed for Dr Mahathir to be given strength to face the ordeal, as well as good health and the continued love and support of his family.
They also prayed for Allah SWT to forgive Dr Siti Hasmah, accept her good deeds and place her among His faithful and righteous servants.
"Thank you too, Kak Hasmah, for all your kindness to us, and certainly our prayers and memories will accompany you in your passing," he said.
Dr Siti Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) this morning at the age of 100 and left behind seven children.
Her remains were
laid to rest
at Pusara Negara, Precinct 20, Putrajaya at 6.20pm today with a state funeral ceremony.

Title: PH, Bersatu in 'table talks' over Melaka election cooperation tonight
Article:
MELAKA: Bersatu and Pakatan Harapan leaders are at a closed-door dinner tonight in what is believed to be a meeting over possible cooperation during the upcoming Melaka election.
Spotted arriving for the dinner at a hotel in Jalan Hang Tuah is being attended by, among others, Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz; the party's state election director Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad; associate wing vice-chief and supreme council member Datuk Seri R. Sanjeevan and Melaka Bersatu information chief Datuk Hishamuddin Abdul Karim.
Also spotted were Melaka Amanah chairman Datuk Ashraf Mukhlis Minghat; acting state PKR chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim and Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia president Datuk Dr Ibrahim Ali.
Hishamuddin, when met, said the meeting was an informal dinner gathering intended as an "introductory session".
"It's also intended to obtain the initial views of all parties regarding the state election.
"However, discussions on cooperation remain open, and there is still room to engage in discussions with all parties," he said.
The media had previously reported that Melaka PH was expected to contest the upcoming state election under a PH Plus formula without the involvement of Barisan Nasional.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari was reported to have said that there had been no negotiations with BN so far, while discussions with several other parties that shared similar aspirations were still ongoing.

Title: Dr Siti Hasmah remembered as gracious, generous by diplomat and admirers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali once spared a young diplomat's blushes when he served a seafood dinner to her husband, who did not care for fish.
The anecdote was shared by retired diplomat Datuk M. Santhananaban in a tribute he wrote and sent to the New Straits Times following her death today.
He said the dinner took place in Hong Kong, where he hosted Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, then the deputy prime minister.
When he offered to order something else, Dr Siti Hasmah stepped in.
"She later told me that we should not fuss unduly about food preferences as there would always be something on the table to eat," he wrote.
He said she always brought a gift for his daughter during visits to Argentina, where he was later posted, signing them as being from "Amachee" (grandmother).
"It was a great privilege for my family and me to have met and known this genial, gracious and generous lady," he said.
Santhananaban was among those who attended the funeral.
Members of the public also turned out to pay their respects, among them Lady Bikers Malaysia president Mira Yaakob.
She said she learned of Dr Siti Hasmah's death from a friend after a work meeting this morning. Her friends had asked her to go on their behalf.
She described Dr Siti Hasmah as an icon and an idol to many, for both her appearance and her personality.
She recalled how warm Dr Siti Hasmah was with the people and with children.
"It's the way she carries herself that is so inspiring," she told the NST.
[[nid:1543339]]
She said her generation had grown up with Dr Siti Hasmah as the wife of the nation's prime minister for more than two decades.
Retiree Fawzia Salem from Cyberjaya said she came as soon as she heard the news.
"We were very saddened when we heard the news. We decided to come immediately because we wanted to pay our last respects.
"She was such a great wife... she was revered for her grace and the support she gave Tun Dr Mahathir (Mohamad)," she said.
Siti Hasmah died
at the National Heart Institute in Kuala Lumpur today, at the age of 100.
She was laid to rest with full state honours at the National Cemetery in Presint 20, Putrajaya.
A pioneering Malay woman doctor, Dr Siti Hasmah is remembered for her
contributions to public health
, particularly maternal and child health.
She was Kedah's first woman medical officer in the field and served twice as the prime minister's wife.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dr Mahathir sheds tears as Siti Hasmah laid to rest [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: After seven decades together, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today faced one of his most difficult moments as he accompanied his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, to her final resting place.
Dr Mahathir, who used a motorised wheelchair and wore an oxygen tube, remained present throughout the funeral rites as family members gathered to pay their last respects.
A sombre atmosphere marked the proceedings, from the family residence and the paying of last respects and funeral prayers at Masjid As-Syarif, Taman Sungai Besi Indah, to the National Cemetery, Precinct 20, Putrajaya.
Looking despondent, the former prime minister was seen gazing blankly for a moment at his wife's remains while paying his last respects at the mosque before joining the funeral prayers, with thousands of congregants filling the mosque and spilling into the surrounding area.
Upon arriving at Pusara Negara, Dr Mahathir watched as his wife's remains were taken to the burial plot before she was laid to rest.
From his motorised wheelchair, he observed the burial in a solemn atmosphere as family members stood close by.
Dr Mahathir was seen shedding tears beside his wife's grave during the final moments, taking a last look at the woman who had shared his life for so many years.
To Malaysians, Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah were not merely a former prime minister and his wife. Their warmth and affection for each other, often displayed in public, endeared them to many.
At official events and during more casual appearances, Dr Siti Hasmah was rarely far from her husband's side, serving as his companion and a pillar of support throughout his life and political career.
The couple's easy-going nature also frequently drew attention through their jokes, teasing and warm interactions, offering a glimpse into the personal side of two people who spent most of their lives together.
Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah tied the knot on Aug 5, 1956 and last August marked their 70th wedding anniversary.
Over the years, Dr Siti Hasmah was not only a wife and mother to their seven children, but also remained by Dr Mahathir's side through various phases of life and his long political career.
Dr Siti Hasmah
died
at the National Heart Institute (IJN) this morning at the age of 100.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: U Mobile leads in 5G speeds, Unifi ranked first for overall video & 5G video experience
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: U Mobile Sdn Bhd has taken the lead in 5G download speeds, with its performance improving significantly to 280 Mbps in the April-June 2026 period from 227 Mbps in August-October 2025, according to CIMB Securities.
The latest Opensignal data puts U Mobile ahead of CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Bhd and Telekom Malaysia Bhd's Unifi Mobile, which recorded 5G download speeds of between 190 Mbps and 235 Mbps.
U Mobile also recorded the highest overall download speed at 107 Mbps, helped by its strong 5G availability.
Its own 5G population coverage rose to 85 per cent in July from 58 per cent at end-October 2025. UM is targeting coverage of 90 per cent in financial year 2027 (FY27) and 95 peer cent in FY28, CIMB Securities said.
The firm said U Mobile had also completed the migration of all its subscribers to its own 5G network ahead of the expiry of its wholesale access agreement with Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) on July 1.
However, U Mobile lead is less clear in other areas of network performance.
Unifi ranked first for both overall video experience and 5G video experience, supported by DNB's 5G network and Maxis' 4G network. U Mobile ranked second, followed by CelcomDigi and Maxis.
The gap between the top and bottom operators was relatively narrow, at eight per cent for overall video experience and just three per cent for 5G video experience.
Unifi also led in overall gaming experience, which reflects network latency, while CelcomDigi ranked first for 5G gaming experience.
The gap between the highest and lowest scores was again small, at three per cent for overall gaming and two per cent for 5G gaming.
For overall coverage experience, CelcomDigi ranked first, followed by Maxis. CIMB Securities said the two operators had a clear advantage over U Mobile and Unifi, likely due to their stronger 4G coverage.
U Mobile, however, made the biggest improvement in consistent quality, rising from fourth place to first.
CIMB Securities said U Mobile had yet to establish a decisive overall network advantage.
It expects DNB's 5G network to improve over the next 12 months as the network deploys an additional 100 MHz of 3.5 GHz spectrum in high-traffic areas.
DNB should also benefit from additional capacity following U Mobile and Unifi's exits from its network.
Still, CIMB Securities expects U Mobile's improving network performance and pricing strategy to help it gain about one percentage point of revenue market share a year over the coming years.
The firm also expects U Mobile to support some recovery in industry pricing, while maintaining its relative pricing against CelcomDigi and Maxis.
This could support slightly stronger mobile industry revenue growth of 2.0-3.0 per cent year-on-year in 2026 and 2027, it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor Sultan, Tengku Permaisuri mourn Siti Hasmah's passing

Title: Tun Dr Hasmah: A fellow Klang girl's personal tribute
Article:
From pioneering doctor to Prime Minister's wife and humanitarian, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali lived through a century of Malaysian history. Elena Koshy remembers a fellow Klang girl whose warmth and kindness left an impression she still treasures.
Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali lived through a century of Malaysian history and carved out a remarkable place in it herself.
Born in Klang in 1926, she came of age in a Malaya very different from the country we know today, living through war, colonial rule, Merdeka and the transformation of modern Malaysia.
One of Malaya's earliest Malay women doctors, she entered the King Edward VII College of Medicine in Singapore in 1947 as the only Malay woman in her cohort and graduated in 1955. She went on to become a pioneer in maternal and child health, taking healthcare into rural communities and devoting much of her professional life to the welfare of women, children and families.
When her husband, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, became Malaysia's fourth Prime Minister in 1981, another chapter began. For the next 22 years, Tun Dr Hasmah occupied one of the most visible roles in the country, standing beside him through some of the most consequential years in modern Malaysian history.
But she was never content simply to stand beside the Prime Minister. A doctor long before she entered Seri Perdana, Tun Dr Hasmah used the platform that came with the role to champion causes close to her heart, particularly women, children, families and public health. She also represented Malaysia internationally, including leading the Malaysian delegation to the United Nations Fourth World Conference on Women in Beijing in 1995.
There was courage beneath that famously gentle manner too. In 2000, she led a group of Malaysian women on a humanitarian mission to Iraq to witness first-hand the devastating effects of sanctions on ordinary people, particularly mothers and children. She visited hospitals and orphanages, brought medical supplies and even found herself being taken to a secret meeting with Saddam Hussein. She later recalled that while she was not afraid, she was "praying hard", telling herself, "Insya Allah, God's with me."
Her memoir,
My Name is Hasmah
, says something important in its very title. "Long before I was known as the wife of the Prime Minister of Malaysia, I was Dr Hasmah," she writes. "And long before I was Dr Hasmah, I was Anak Pak Ali Bankrap. Along the way, some people — seven to be exact — started calling me 'Mummy'."
There is so much of her in those few lines: the humour, the humility and the quiet insistence on being remembered as a person in her own right.
My Name is Hasmah
is her story told in her own voice, looking back on an extraordinary life and the Malaysia that changed around her.
She was brilliant, brave, curious and extraordinarily accomplished. Yet of all the things I choose to remember about Tun Dr Hasmah, I remember her kindness.
I had the privilege of meeting her at her home some years ago. She played the violin and piano for us, laughed and chatted with us and had that rare ability to make an occasion that could have felt intimidating feel warm and wonderfully ordinary.
And yes, the Klang girl in me was ridiculously happy that this extraordinary woman was a fellow Klang girl too.
The year before, I had received an MPI Gold award for Best Feature Article for a piece on Tan Sri Dr Noor Hisham Abdullah. What touched me was that Tun Dr Hasmah remembered the story. She congratulated me and told me how pleased she was that I had written about him.
For someone who had met countless people over an extraordinary public life to remember something that mattered so much to me meant more than she could have known.
Before I left that day, she signed my copy of
My Name is Hasmah.
I was thrilled to have it then. Today, I find myself looking at that signature rather differently. A book I already treasured has become something far more precious, a little piece of that afternoon that I get to keep.
Perhaps that was why Malaysians loved her so. For all the titles, accolades and decades spent close to power, there remained something warm, maternal and wonderfully human about her.
She was a doctor, humanitarian, advocate, musician, wife, mother, grandmother and great-grandmother. But to generations of us, she also felt a little like a mum to Malaysia.
Rest well, Tun Dr Hasmah. Malaysia has lost a remarkable woman and a precious link to a century of our history.
And from one Klang girl to another, I am so very glad I have my little keepsake of you, and even more grateful that, for one lovely afternoon, I had the privilege of knowing the woman behind the name.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tioman slipway gets safety upgrade by Telekom Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: At the southern tip of Pulau Tioman, a weathered slipway in Kampung Mukut has been given a new lease of life with Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) upgrading the facility to provide safer access for young sailors.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan launched the upgraded facility, which replaces the ageing structure that had raised safety concerns for users, particularly students undergoing sailing training.
The new facility gives students a safer point to handle boats and sailing equipment, helping support the development of young sailing talent on the island.
The initiative is part of TM's Future Skills programme, which aims to take learning beyond the classroom.
The sailing talent development programme involves students from all four schools on Pulau Tioman, with technical guidance from the Malaysia Sailing Association.
Amir Hamzah launched the facility during his working visit to the village to review the implementation and progress of the Kampung Angkat Madani initiative on Pulau Tioman.
Kampung Mukut is TM's adopted village and the starting point of its Jangkau Digital TM initiative in 2025.
TM group chief executive officer Datuk Amar Huzaimi Md Deris said the initiative aims to use digital progress to create more opportunities for children, support local entrepreneurs, strengthen communities and preserve Tioman's environment and heritage.
"This reflects TM's greater purpose - ensuring that digital progress is not simply about the technology we build, but about how it empowers people and creates opportunities for a better future.
"Our experience in Mukut provides us with a foundation to extend this impact further across Tioman," he said.
Among the initiatives are the implementation of MasjidNet across all five mosques on Pulau Tioman, digital training for micro, small and medium enterprises, and the Usahawan Digital TM programme for eligible B40 entrepreneurs.
TM is also conducting a biodiversity baseline study with local universities and working with the Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute to preserve the mangga dodol, a local heritage variety in Kampung Mukut.

Title: China, US agree tariff cuts on US$60bil of goods including agriculture, household items
Article:
BEIJING: China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on US$60 billion worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys.
Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended US$30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday.
For the United States, that was "unlocking improved market access" for about 30 per cent of US exports to China, he said.
The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week.
One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It did not include soybeans.
Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices.
In another list were Washington's reciprocal tariff cuts for Chinese small appliances such as coffee makers and toasters, tableware, blankets and bed linens.
The lists also included toys, fireworks, artificial flowers, Christmas tree lamps and other holiday decorations, and children's car seats.
LONGER TRADE TRUCE
China's commerce ministry said on Monday a two-month extension of a trade truce with the United States through to January 10 would provide room for both sides to evaluate their ongoing arrangement to resolve economic and trade issues, while considering how to advance on those fronts.
The extension also provides a "relatively stable and predictable policy environment" for cooperation among companies and continued active discussions.
Both sides will hold regular talks on potential investment opportunities and barriers, enhancing policy transparency and predictability, and responding to enterprises' concerns, the ministry said.
Stocks fell sharply in China on Monday, with investors having few concrete details to cheer from the leaders' summit and underlying tensions resurfacing. Technology stocks fell on a bipartisan US push to ban Chinese components from data centres and the benchmark blue-chip index slid more than two per cent to a one-year low.
AGRICULTURE AND COAL
China's choice of products for tariff cuts looks designed to help Beijing meet what the White House says is a US$17-billion commitment to buy agricultural goods. China has already resumed large-scale buying of US soybeans under a deal struck last year to buy 25 million metric tons annually.
Both countries will set up an agriculture working group under a trade council, which will hold its first meeting before the year ends to discuss two-way market access and regulation, the commerce ministry said.
The presidential summit also yielded an agreement for China to import 10 million metric tons of coal annually from the United States in 2027 and 2028, the White House release showed. That amount roughly equals 2 per cent of China's coal imports each year.
Liquefied natural gas and oil were not on the list.
"Importing US coal is not only a beneficial supplement to China's domestic coal market, but also brings stable economic income and employment to the US coal industry," the Chinese ministry said.
AI, FINANCIAL FIRMS AND DIRECT FLIGHTS
On artificial intelligence, both sides have agreed on a communication channel for incidents and will hold a follow-up dialogue by the end of November.
China will also examine and approve foreign financial services institutions, including those with US capital, to conduct business and open branches in China.
There will also be continued communication on increasing flights between China and the United States, the ministry statement said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'She was ready to leave us all,' says Mukhriz
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali had been receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN) since Saturday and was still cheerful when her family visited her last night, said Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir.
Mukhriz said his mother was being treated for another ailment and in good spirits.
"She was in a good mood ..but she told us she was ready to leave us all," he said.
He said he was informed by the hospital at 8am today that Dr Siti Hasmah had suffered a heart-related episode, prompting him to rush to IJN.
When he arrived, medical specialists were performing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on his mother before she was transferred to the Coronary Care Unit.
Mukhriz said the family was informed at 9am that CPR would continue for another 15 minutes and would be stopped if her heart did not resume functioning.
He said his father, former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, was also at IJN at the time, in a separate room.
Mukhriz said his mother had always prioritised service to the people and nation and continued to think about the country's future until the final stages of her life.
He said the family was fortunate to have had her for so many years, adding that her longevity was a meaningful blessing for the family and the country.
Meanwhile, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir said the family was shocked by Dr Siti Hasmah's sudden passing.
He said the family had been able to spend considerable time with her in the months, weeks and days leading up to her death.
"There's no one last memory. There are millions of memories," Mokhzani said, recalling the many family gatherings they had shared in recent months.
Mokhzani also thanked the armed forces, police and Putrajaya officials for ensuring the funeral arrangements proceeded smoothly, from IJN to the family home, mosque and National Cemetery.
He said the family was grateful that relatives, friends and the public were able to pay their respects.
Mokhzani said a tahlil ceremony would be held at the family home tonight after Isyak, with further prayers expected over the following days.
Dr Siti Hasmah was
laid to rest
with full state honours at the National Cemetery in Precinct 20, Putrajaya, after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that she would be accorded a state funeral.
A pioneering Malay woman doctor, Siti Hasmah is remembered for her contributions to
public health
, particularly maternal and child health.
She was Kedah's first female medical officer in the field and served twice as the prime minister's wife.

Title: Fadhlina: Education Ministry has strengthened anti-bullying measures, but 'work isn't done'
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Education Ministry has strengthened measures to address bullying, including increasing hostel supervision, improving complaints channels and expanding CCTV coverage.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said her ministry had introduced measures over several years while adding new initiatives to address remaining gaps.
"I understand parents' concerns whenever a bullying case occurs. I am also a mother. My own child has studied and stayed in a hostel under the same education system.
"Every time parents send their children to school, there is a trust we carry together. They want their children to return home safely. We cannot take that trust lightly.
"Whenever a case occurs, we must have the courage to review what remains weak. If there are gaps, we fix them. I do not want us to be complacent with what has already been done.
"As long as there are children who do not yet feel safe at school, our work is not finished," she said in a posting on Facebook.
It was reported that a Form Two student at a school in the Kuala Pilah district in Negri Sembilan died recently, reportedly
after being bullied
at the school hostel.
The 14-year-old was found unconscious at the school hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital (HTAN), where he was pronounced dead.
Fadhlina said among the measures introduced or expanded were the deployment of 300 short term employment (MySTEP) assistant wardens from April 2026 to help monitor hostel students, particularly at night.
She said the ministry also enhanced its bullying complaints system by introducing an anonymous complaint function through the Bullying Complaints Portal to protect the identities of complainants and witnesses.
"The ministry is also working with the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department on the drafting of the Anti-Bullying Act 2026, which includes the establishment of an Anti-BullyingTribunal as a channel for victims to seek redress.
"CCTV installation has also been expanded in residential schools. A total of 200 boarding schools were equipped with CCTV in 2025, while installation in 333 boarding schools is being expanded in 2026 with an additional allocation of RM5 million," she added.
Fadhlina said the Guidelines for Managing Bullying Misconduct, introduced in 2023, provided schools with an official reference for receiving complaints, conducting investigations, taking disciplinary action and implementing interventions.
Meanwhile, she said Character Education would be introduced under the 2027 school curriculum, with emphasis on values and character including integrity and empathy.
She added that the ministry was also implementing the SAFE framework, which focused on prevention, early intervention and rehabilitation through measures including peer support and focused counselling.
"Efforts to address bullying must continue as long as students remained at risk," she stressed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maybank completes RM2.5bil AT1 sukuk mudharabah issuance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5 billion additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750 million, RM1.10 billion and RM650 million, respectively.
The RM750 million tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.10 billion tranche carries a rate of 5.11 per cent until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033.
Meanwhile, the RM650 million tranche has a fixed distribution rate of 5.15 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 26, 2036.
"The relevant reset distribution rates for the three tranches are based on the prevailing five-year, seven-year and 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rates, respectively, plus their respective initial spreads for fixed rates of 0.98 per cent, 0.97 per cent and 0.98 per cent per annum," said Maybank.
The proceeds would be used for shariah-compliant purposes, including investments in ringgit- and foreign currency-denominated Islamic financial instruments approved by Bank Negara Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council or the Securities Commission Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council.
It would also be used to fund the Islamic business activities of Maybank's subsidiaries and overseas branches, as well as other shariah-compliant business activities, said Maybank.
The returns from the investments would be used for the periodic distributions of the AT1 sukuk mudharabah, which are payable semi-annually.
The sukuk has been assigned an AA3 rating by RAM Rating Services Bhd.
